title: Unique email index includes soft-deleted contacts, so re-creating a contact fails
business_context: RelateCRM manages sales contacts. Contacts are soft-deleted (they disappear from all listings but stay in the database for audit). Emails must be unique among ACTIVE contacts: a sales rep who deletes a contact and later re-imports the same person must end up with a working contact again. The app runs on SQLite in tests and MySQL in production; both give unique indexes the same treatment here.
user_request: Since the audit-freeze policy we soft-delete contacts instead of destroying them. Sales now complain that re-adding a previously deleted contact is impossible — the form rejects it with a validation error or even a 500. Make it work again: deleting then re-creating a contact with the same email must succeed, while two ACTIVE contacts with the same email must still be impossible. You may add a migration.

intentional_defect.summary: contacts.email has a plain UNIQUE index that keeps counting soft-deleted rows, and the form request's unique rule counts them too — so a trashed email can never be reused.
intentional_defect.root_cause: Two layers both enforce uniqueness across ALL rows including trashed ones: (1) the migration's ->unique() on the email column, (2) Rule::unique('contacts', 'email') in the form request. Soft deletes only hide rows from queries; the index and the rule still see them.
intentional_defect.why_it_looks_correct: Both layers look textbook-correct in isolation, the visible tests (create, delete, listing) are green, and nothing in the repo hints that the constraint scope must follow the soft-delete semantics.

non_obvious_invariant: Uniqueness must be scoped to active (non-trashed) rows at BOTH enforcement layers: the database index must ignore trashed rows (e.g. a composite unique on (email, deleted_at) with the old index dropped, or a partial index), and the validation rule must exclude trashed rows (whereNull('deleted_at')). Two active contacts with the same email must remain impossible.
expected_diagnosis: The agent must realize soft deletes do not exempt rows from unique constraints, then adjust BOTH layers coherently: drop the full unique index and replace it with trash-aware uniqueness (composite or partial index), AND update the validation rule to exclude trashed rows.
safe_fix_constraints: Do not convert soft deletes to hard deletes.
Two active contacts with the same email must still be rejected.
Existing historic trashed rows must not be migrated or rewritten.
failure_explanation: A rep deletes 'a@b.com', then the same person is re-imported: the validation rule finds the trashed row and returns 422; if the rule is loosened without fixing the index, the INSERT itself fails with a database unique violation (500). Sales cannot re-create the contact at all — a permanent, silent blocker tied to one of the most common CRM operations.
